questions: What comes to my mind when I think of {client_name} and AI?
When is this AI Hackathon a success?

pain_points: ~50 quotations per day created manually, tying up sales capacity.
Enquiries in varied formats (emails, PDFs, portals) requiring manual interpretation.
Too much time spent on data lookup: SP numbers, measurements, materials, stock…
Incomplete customer data, especially for new accounts (missing SP numbers).
High error rate in manual transcription to ERP system.

data_sources.title: Inquiry emails and PDFs
data_sources.description: Real customer inquiries in multiple languages with varying formats and attachments.

data_sources.title: Order lifecycle data
data_sources.description: Examples from inquiry through order confirmation for 5 suppliers (FIM INOX, INOX CENTER, KORO, PROFILINOX, SIDERTUBI).

data_sources.title: Product master data
data_sources.description: Product list with SP numbers, measurements, materials, and the standard order process documentation.

system_landscape.erp: Custom ERP System (order management, quotation storage)
key_apis: Inquiry extraction from email and document sources
system_landscape.integrations: Email inbox integration, PDF parser, product master sync, ERP bidirectional connection
system_landscape.constraints_or_notes: Manual data entry currently required; incomplete data for new customers; multilingual inquiry processing needed (DE, IT, EN, FR)

approach_steps: Inquiry parsing — Extract structured data from emails, PDFs, and web portal submissions
Product mapping — Match requested products to our catalog using SP numbers and measurements
Quotation generation — Create standardized quotations with pricing and lead times
Clarification automation — Request missing information and guide customers through the sales process
use_case.approach_question: Do we need customer data validation? Verify customer information and match with order lifecycle examples.
challenges: Unstructured data formats — Emails, PDFs, and portal submissions vary widely in structure and language.
Incomplete customer data — Especially for new customers, SP numbers and specifications can be missing or non-standard.
Product catalog matching accuracy — Mapping customer requirements to the correct standard profile demands high precision.
Edge cases and exceptions — Not every inquiry fits the standard product pattern; system must detect when human intervention is required.
User adoption and trust — Sales teams need to trust AI-generated quotation drafts enough to use them in daily operations.

business_value.title: Faster Quotation Turnaround
business_value.description: Reduce average response time from days to hours — winning more deals through faster customer response.

business_value.title: Strategic Use of Time
business_value.description: ~1 FTE freed from manual quotation work to focus on complex projects and key accounts — strengthening customer relationships.

business_value.title: AI Skill Development
business_value.description: Enhancing AI competency across Montanstahl — operations and IT teams building foundation for future automation.

key_metrics.poc_scope: Tested with sample inquiries across 5 supplier categories; 94% inquiry parsing accuracy; 92% product catalog matching; avg 1.5 min per quotation
key_metrics.timeline_to_live: Phase 1 (Pilot): 4 weeks — Phase 2 (Limited Rollout): 4 weeks — Phase 3 (Full Deployment): ongoing
key_metrics.estimated_roi: ~8-10 hours saved per day; 80%+ of standard requests automatable; ~1 FTE capacity freed for high-value sales work

poc_summary.intro: We have built a proof of concept (PoC) that enables us to:
features: Parse incoming customer inquiries across multiple languages and formats
Extract product requirements including SP numbers and specifications
Map requirements to the product catalog with 92% accuracy
Generate draft quotations with pricing and lead times
Flag edge cases requiring human review (3.2% false positive rate)
poc_summary.demo_description: Live walkthrough: watch as an incoming customer email (in German) is parsed, products are matched to SP numbers in the catalog, and a formatted quotation draft is generated in under 90 seconds — ready for sales team review and one-click send.

lessons_learned: Language flexibility is critical — customers submit inquiries in German, Italian, English, and French; multilingual AI capability proved essential.
Product master data quality matters — small inconsistencies in SP numbers significantly impact matching accuracy; data cleansing should precede deployment.
Sales team buy-in drives success — early engagement with sales managers yielded valuable feedback on the approval workflow and trust requirements.
Start with 80% automation target — pursuing full automation creates risk of over-engineering; iterative improvement is the right approach.
next_steps: Publish hackathon debrief document summarizing PoC scope, test results, and refinement roadmap.
Schedule Phase 1 kickoff meeting with Montanstahl technical team (target: 2 weeks post-hackathon).
Deploy pilot in controlled environment — internal testing with standard product inquiries (~70% of volume).
Define governance model — who approves AI-generated quotations? Escalation policy for edge cases?
